title: "Honor of Kings had its biggest year yet": As HoK grows outside of China, the PC vs. mobile MOBA clash is heating up
summary: "Honor of Kings had its biggest year yet": As HoK grows outside of China, the PC vs. mobile MOBA clash is heating up  Esports Insider
content:
Paul Delos Santos is a reporter based in Las Vegas. He covers the Vegas Golden Knights forNHL.comand also covers esports and general Las Vegas sports for The Sporting Tribune. He’s a gamer who never has time to play them, so he naturally opted to write and talk about them instead.

Olivia Richman is a seasoned esports journalist who has worked with Inven Global, Esports Illustrated, Esports.gg, and more. As an editor and writer at Esports Insider, she loves telling unique esports stories, especially within the FGC. When not working and gaming, Olivia loves collecting Kirby plush, eating sushi, and driving her cars at the track.

It’s easy to know thatLeague of Legends, with its immense history and popularity, is the most watched MOBA in the world. In 2025 alone, more than 735.9 million watch hours of League of Legends content were viewed by fans, according to Esports Charts.

Mobile Legends: Bang Bang, League’s mobile cousin, ranked second in MOBA with 435.1 million watch hours.

Honor of Kings, another mobile MOBA, is fourth, trailing behind the top two and MOBA staple DOTA 2 in the watch hour rankings. Even though it trails massively behind the other three games (Honor of Kings has failed to crack the 100 million watch hour mark), it is receiving a bit of buzz recently.

“2025 was a record year specifically for the mobile MOBAs,” Esports Charts co-founder and CEO Artyom Odintsov told Esports Insider. “Both MLBB’s M7 World Championship and the Honor of Kings World Cup hit new all-time highs in hours watched and peak viewers, while League’s last all-time record was set back in 2024, and Dota 2’s in 2021.”
